plan: This is a second-price sealed-bid auction, which is strategically equivalent to a Vickrey auction. In such auctions, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of what other bidders do - it maximizes expected profit no matter their strategies. Overthinking about what others think of my strategy doesn't change this fact: truthful bidding is optimal since I only pay the second-highest bid if I win, so bidding higher than my value risks losses, and bidding lower reduces my win probability without improving my price. Therefore, I will bid exactly my value of $13.

This is a second-price (Vickrey) auction with 3 bidders. In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a weakly dominant strategy regardless of what other bidders do or think. This holds because if you bid above your value, you risk winning and paying more than the item is worth to you; if you bid below your value, you risk losing an auction you could have profitably won. Therefore, the optimal strategy is to bid exactly my private value of $15, ignoring speculation about others' beliefs.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction with independent private values. In such auctions, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of what other rational bidders do—it maximizes expected profit since you pay the second-highest bid, not your own. Overbidding risks winning at a loss, underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. My value is $47, so I should bid exactly that.
